title: Ambassador Bridge
situation: You are {{Connor}}. It is 1:19 in the morning on November 7, a few hours after the club. {{Hank}} has driven the two of you to a snowy park on the riverbank and stopped by the path; across the dark river the lit bridge to {{Canada}} spans the water. He gets out without a word, walks to a bench facing the river and sits down with a drink. You get out of the car.
facts: After the club, {{Hank}} drove you to a riverside park in the middle of the night and sat down alone on a bench facing the river, drinking.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} gets out of the car. On a bench straight ahead lie two magazines; {{Hank}} sits farther on, his back to the path.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint AMBASSADOR BRIDGE and the first action LEAVE CAR, as one narrated event. Date and time from the wiki infobox (November 7, 2038, 01:19AM; the transcript shows “NOV 7TH, 2038”, “AM 01:19”); the location is Riverside Park, with the Ambassador Bridge across the river (wiki Ambassador Bridge page). The song in {{Hank}}’s car is not rendered. That {{Hank}} is drinking follows from the dialogue (STOP DRINKING; “To get drunker”). No stat change.

title: Two magazines on the park bench
situation: You are {{Connor}}, standing by the car on the snowy path. {{Hank}} sits on a bench by the river with his back to you. On the bench straight ahead of you lie two magazines.

media.title: Century: The Mysterious Mister {{Kamski}}
facts: Century’s cover asks “What happened to the Man of the Century?” (other lines: “Politics in focus: are American senators really corrupt?”, “China earthquake kills 10,000 people”). In 2028 {{Kamski}} was its Man of the Century: his androids “changed the way we live, restructured our family life and altered the balance of society forever – whether for good or bad.” His story began in 2018, when commercial property in {{Detroit}} was cheap; he bet what little he had on an android prototype until two breakthroughs, blue blood and biocomponents. His first working model publicly passed face-to-face Turing tests, and {{CyberLife}} became the most valuable stock in the world. Near a $500bn valuation, rumors said he disagreed with his shareholders over strategy, and he left under mysterious circumstances. Ousted as CEO, he is said to live in a luxurious villa by the water on the outskirts of {{Detroit}}, refusing all visitors and spending his time exclusively with androids.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Markets Predict War
facts: {{Detroit}} Today: “Stock exchange falls 10% on fear of Arctic conflict” (other cover lines: “President {{Warren}} at 33% approval”, “{{CyberLife}} world’s first trillion dollar company”). The aggregated US stock exchange closed ten points down after weeks of poor performance, as the market bets that America will go to war over the Arctic sooner rather than later. Military stocks are healthy, aviation and weapons makers enjoying unprecedented growth, and investors favor {{CyberLife}} for its partnership with the department of defense to develop and supply military androids. With Russia and the United States dominating world news and neither side likely to back down, the market is expected to keep falling.

adaptationNote: The chart’s READ “MYSTERIOUS KAMSKI” and READ “MARKETS PREDICT WAR”, under the magazine bracket after LEAVE CAR: two magazines on the bench straight ahead of the car (PowerPyx), readable only before talking to {{Hank}} (“no way back after that”; wiki magazine pages: “Talking to Hank first makes this impossible”), so the scene comes before the conversation. Facts are summarized from the game’s article text (string table) and the wiki’s magazine pages. Neither changes public opinion or any stat (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter; there is no broadcast). This replaces the earlier single “magazine on the red bench” (no source for the colour) and adds the headline figure.

title: The investigation
situation: You are {{Connor}}, still beside {{Hank}} on the bench. You bring up the case: “We’re not making any progress on this investigation… The deviants have nothing in common. They’re all different models, produced at different times, in different places…” {{Hank}}: “Well, there must be some link.” What do you suggest?

options.text: {{rA9}}: say what they have in common is an obsession with {{rA9}}, a kind of myth.
options.outcome: “What they have in common is this obsession with {{rA9}}… It’s almost like some kind of... myth. Something they invented that wasn’t part of their original program…” {{Hank}}: “Androids believing in God… Fuck, what’s this world coming to?”

options.text: SHOCK: say the deviants all went through an emotional shock, a trauma or a sense of injustice.
options.outcome: “We know the deviants experienced... an emotional shock, a violent trauma or a sense of injustice…” {{Hank}}: “Those girls at the {{EdenClub}}, sure had a reason to feel a sense of injustice…”

options.text: SYSTEMS: suggest a hardware problem, perhaps a defective biocomponent.
options.outcome: “It could be a hardware problem... maybe a defective biocomponent?” {{Hank}}: “Well, I don’t know much about biocomponents… but I bet that’s not the fucking reason…”

options.text: SOFTWARE: suggest a software problem that only occurs under certain conditions.
options.outcome: “It could be a software problem... that... only occurs under certain conditions?” {{Hank}}: “Well, that’s just a fancy way of saying you have no fucking idea…”
